# Expected values: BigQuery's TRUNC definition (toward zero, including negative N),
# NULL propagation and nonfinite examples:
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/mathematical_functions.md
# Precision-sensitive FLOAT64 cases recorded from BigQuery are in trunc_boundaries.txt.

SELECT CAST(TRUNC(x) AS INT64) FROM UNNEST([2.3]) x
=> "2"

SELECT CAST(TRUNC(x) AS INT64) FROM UNNEST([-2.8]) x
=> "-2"

SELECT TRUNC(x, 1) FROM UNNEST([2.35]) x
=> "2.3"

SELECT TRUNC(x, 1) FROM UNNEST([-2.35]) x
=> "-2.3"

SELECT CAST(TRUNC(x, -1) AS INT64) FROM UNNEST([123.75]) x
=> "120"

SELECT CAST(TRUNC(x, -1) AS INT64) FROM UNNEST([-123.75]) x
=> "-120"

SELECT TRUNC(x, CAST(NULL AS INT64)) FROM UNNEST([2.35]) x
=> null

SELECT TRUNC(x, 1) FROM UNNEST([CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)]) x
=> null

SELECT TRUNC(x, CAST(NULL AS INT64)) FROM UNNEST([CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)]) x
=> null

SELECT IS_INF(TRUNC(x, 1)) FROM UNNEST([CAST('+inf' AS FLOAT64)]) x
=> "true"

SELECT TRUNC(x, -1) < 0 FROM UNNEST([CAST('-inf' AS FLOAT64)]) x
=> "true"

SELECT IS_NAN(TRUNC(x, 1)) FROM UNNEST([CAST('NaN' AS FLOAT64)]) x
=> "true"

SELECT SAFE.TRUNC(x, 1) FROM UNNEST([-2.35]) x
=> "-2.3"

SELECT TYPEOF(TRUNC(x, 1)) FROM UNNEST([2.35]) x
=> "FLOAT64"
